fields.title: Bone cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Bone cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Bone cancer is a serious condition that may take the form of primary bone tumours or of metastases from other parts of the body. Israel uses innovative methods of diagnosing and treating bone cancer, aimed at improving both the outlook and patients' quality of life.

Diagnosis of bone cancer:

  1. X-rays:
    The first method for identifying changes in the structure of the bones.
  2. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    Assesses how far the bones and soft tissues are affected.
  3. Computed tomography (CT):
    Used for a more detailed study of bone structure and to identify small lesions.
  4. Bone scan:
    A radioactive substance is given to identify cancer cells in the bones.
  5. PET-CT:
    An integrated approach combining PET and CT to assess the metabolic activity of the tumour and search for metastases.
  6. Biopsy:
    Definitive confirmation of the presence of cancer cells in the bone.

Treatments for bone cancer:

  1. Surgery:
    • Resection of the tumour: Removal of the tumour together with some of the surrounding healthy tissue.
    • Limb-sparing surgery: A technique that allows the limb to be preserved when the tumour is removed.
    • Amputation: Used where the tumour is too large or too awkwardly placed for the limb to be preserved.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • Used to destroy cancer cells and reduce the risk of recurrence, particularly after surgery or where an operation is not possible.
  3. Chemotherapy:
    • Used to treat bone cancer, particularly in aggressive and metastatic forms of the disease.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy:
    • The use of modern medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the tumour.
    • Immunotherapy to activate the patient's own immune system to fight the cancer.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Specialists from different fields of medicine work together to create the most effective treatment plan.
  • Advanced medical equipment: The use of the latest advances in medical technology and treatment techniques.
  • An individual approach: Treatment plans are adapted to the particular patient, taking account of the stage of the disease, general health and other important factors.

Treatment of bone cancer in Israel aims for maximum effectiveness, the preservation of function and quality of life, and the minimisation of side effects and the risk of recurrence.

fields.title: Lung cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Lung cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Lung cancer is one of the most serious cancers and requires a comprehensive and individualised approach to treatment. Israeli clinics offer advanced methods of diagnosing and treating lung cancer, combining highly qualified specialists, modern technology and an individual approach to every patient.

Diagnosis of lung cancer

  1. Computed tomography (CT)
    of the chest allows a tumour to be identified at an early stage.
  2. PET-CT
    allows tumours and metastases to be detected and their activity and extent assessed. It helps show how the tumour is responding to treatment.
  3. Bronchoscopy with biopsy
    makes it possible to obtain tissue samples for histological analysis.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  4. Laboratory tests
    include blood tests and cancer markers that help in diagnosis.
  5. Consultation with a specialist
    is needed to establish the best treatment strategy.

Treatment of lung cancer

  1. Surgery
    involves removing the tumour together with part of the lung. Israel uses both traditional operations and minimally invasive methods, including video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS).
  2. Chemotherapy
    is used to destroy cancer cells, both before and after surgery, and as the main treatment in advanced stages.
  3. Targeted therapy
    is directed at particular mutations in the cancer cells, which makes treatment more effective and produces fewer side effects.
  4. Immunotherapy activates the patient's own immune system to fight the cancer cells.
  5. Radiotherapy
    is used on its own and in combination with other treatments to destroy cancer cells and shrink the tumour.

Why patients choose Israel

Israel attracts patients from all over the world thanks to its advanced approach to treating lung cancer. Highly qualified specialists, the use of the latest medical technology and an individual approach to every patient offer strong prospects of successful treatment. Patients also value the comprehensive approach to treatment, with support at every stage — from diagnosis through to rehabilitation afterwards — and the opportunity to receive the newest therapies, take part in clinical trials and access innovative treatments that may not be available in other countries.

fields.title: Uterine cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Uterine cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the womb accounts for a significant share of cancers in women. The latest medical advances are available in Israel, aimed at effective treatment and at improving patients' quality of life.

Diagnosis of uterine cancer

  1. Transvaginal ultrasound
    Gives more accurate images of the internal structure of the womb.
  2. Hysteroscopy:
    A miniature camera is introduced into the cavity of the womb through the vagina and cervix, allowing the doctor to examine the inner surface of the womb and take tissue samples for a biopsy.
  3. Biopsy:
    Examination of tissue samples, which confirms the presence of cancer cells.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  4. PET-CT
    Assesses how far the cancer has spread and whether there are metastases.
  5. Laboratory tests
    Full blood count, biochemistry and blood tests for the relevant tumour markers.
  6. Consultation with a specialist
    To develop an individual treatment strategy (treatment may begin with a consultation with an oncologist or a surgeon).

Treatments for uterine cancer

  1. Surgery
    Israel makes wide use of both traditional operations and minimally invasive surgical techniques. One example is surgery using the da Vinci robot, which allows the operation to be carried out with great precision and minimal risk to the patient. Hysterectomy (removal of the womb) is recommended depending on the stage and extent of the disease.
  2. Hormone therapy with progestin
    Used to slow the growth of the tumour, particularly in certain types of uterine cancer. This method can be effective as an addition to other treatments.
  3. Radiotherapy
    Includes external beam radiotherapy and brachytherapy (internal irradiation). These methods are aimed at destroying cancer cells and preventing the disease from recurring.
  4. Chemotherapy and radiotherapy
    A combination of these methods is often used to treat advanced stages of uterine cancer. Chemotherapy fights the cancer cells throughout the body, while radiotherapy is directed at destroying cells in a particular area.

Every treatment plan in Israel is drawn up carefully, taking account of many factors including the type of cancer, its stage, the patient's general health and her personal preferences. Particular attention is given not only to fighting the disease but also to preserving the patient's quality of life and to support and rehabilitation after treatment.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of uterine cancer

Israeli clinics are known for their advanced methods of treating uterine cancer, and attract patients from all over the world thanks to a number of key advantages:

  • Highly qualified specialists
    Israeli oncologists and gynaecologists have international experience and use the most modern approaches to treatment.
  • Advanced equipment
    The use of the newest technology, including the da Vinci robotic system, allows minimally invasive operations that speed up patients' recovery.
  • An individual approach
    Treatment is planned with each patient's particular circumstances in mind, which makes the therapy as effective as possible.
  • A multidisciplinary approach
    Specialists from various fields take part in treatment, which helps address the problem comprehensively.
  • Innovative treatments: Patients have access to the newest treatment protocols, including targeted therapy and immunotherapy.
  • Comprehensive support
    Care for patients at every stage of treatment, including help with arranging their stay and with rehabilitation.

These factors make Israel the preferred choice for those seeking effective, high-quality treatment for uterine cancer.

fields.title: Bladder cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Bladder cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Bladder cancer is one of the more common cancers. In Israel, patients are offered a comprehensive approach to treating this disease, combining innovative methods of diagnosis and treatment.

Diagnosis of bladder cancer:

  1. Laboratory tests:
    Full blood count, biochemistry, tumour markers and urine tests
  2. Cystoscopy:
    Visual examination of the inner surface of the bladder using a cystoscope.
  3. Ultrasound scan:
    Imaging of the bladder and detection of growths.
  4. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    Detailed assessment of the tumour, its size and extent.
  5. CT urography:
    CT with a contrast medium that concentrates in the urinary system, for highly accurate diagnosis.
  6. Biopsy or review of pathology material:
    Obtaining and analysing tissue samples to confirm the diagnosis.

Treatments for bladder cancer in Israel:

  • Transurethral resection (TUR) followed by intravesical chemotherapy:
    • The cost of the operation includes routine pre-operative preparation (ECG, chest X-ray, consultation with an anaesthetist), the surgical procedure and up to 2 days in hospital, consumables and equipment, express biopsy and pathology examination.
  • Radical resection of the bladder with simultaneous reconstruction:
    • Includes all the items of pre-operative preparation, the surgical procedure and up to 9 days in hospital. After discharge the patient must remain in Israel for 10 days for follow-up.
  • Ureteral reimplantation:
    • The cost of the operation includes routine pre-operative preparation, the surgical procedure and up to 5 days in hospital, together with the necessary consumables and express biopsy. After discharge it is recommended that the patient remain in Israel for follow-up for 10 days.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Oncologists, urologists, radiologists and surgeons combine their efforts to develop the best treatment strategy.
  • Advanced technology: The use of the most modern methods of diagnosis and treatment, delivering high accuracy and a minimal risk of complications.
  • An individualised treatment plan: Treatments are chosen with the stage of the disease, the patient's general health and their preferences in mind.
  • Comprehensive support: Including help with rehabilitation and psychological support at every stage of treatment.

Treatment of bladder cancer in Israel gives patients access to high-quality medical care and innovative treatments, which makes it possible to achieve the best results.
